chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi told us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Ali ibn Awf al-Azdi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Openhandedness (al-sakhā') is that the servant's soul elevates above seeking the forbidden (haram); if he achieves the permissible (halal), his soul is pleased to spend it in the obedience of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual definition of openhandedness (sakhā') in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines openhandedness (sakhā') as an internal spiritual disposition rather than mere material generosity, emphasizing that the soul finds true peace (ṭayyib nafs) only when it rejects the forbidden (ḥarām) and willingly spends permissible wealth in obedience to God. This definition aligns with the Shia emphasis on the purity of intention (ikhlāṣ) and the moral quality of the source of wealth, distinguishing it from superficial charity. The narration highlights that true generosity is rooted in a soul purified from the desire for the forbidden, making the act of spending a form of worship itself.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hussain Sa’d-Abadi, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad bin Nadhr, from Ali bin ‘Awf al-Azdi, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

Openhandedness is that a servant’s soul elevates above seeking the forbidden, and if he achieves the permissible, his soul appeals to spend it in (what brings about) the obedience to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He).
